Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-awakened One.

Khuddakanikāye

The Khuddaka Nikāya

Jātakapāḷi

The Jātaka Pāḷi

(Paṭhamo bhāgo)

(First Part)

1. Ekakanipāto

1. The Book of the Ones

1. Apaṇṇakavaggo

1. The Chapter on the Infallible

1. Apaṇṇakajātakaṃ

1. The Infallible Jātaka

1.

1.

Apaṇṇakaṃ [T 1.0001][V 1.0001][M 1.0001] ṭhānameke, dutiyaṃ āhu takkikā;

Etadaññāya medhāvī, taṃ gaṇhe yadapaṇṇakanti taṃ gaṇheyya apaṇṇakaṃ (ka.).

Some took the infallible position; but those who were speculators took the second. The wise one, having understood this, should take that which is infallible.

Apaṇṇakajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Apaṇṇaka Jātaka, the First.

2. Vaṇṇupathajātakaṃ

2. The Vaṇṇupatha Jātaka

2.

2.

Akilāsuno [V 1.0002] vaṇṇupathe vaṇṇapathe (ka.) khaṇantā, udaṅgaṇe tattha papaṃ avinduṃ;

Evaṃ munī vīriya muni viriya (pī.), muni vīriya (syā. ka.) balūpapanno, akilāsu vinde hadayassa santinti.

The unwearying, digging in the sandy path, found water there in the open ground. Even so the unwearying sage, endowed with the strength of effort, finds peace of heart.

Vaṇṇupathajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Vaṇṇupatha Jātaka, the Second.

3. Serivavāṇijajātakaṃ

3. The Seriva Merchant Jātaka

3.

3.

Idha [T 1.0002][M 1.0002] ce naṃ idha ce hi naṃ (sī. pī.) virādhesi, saddhammassa niyāmataṃ niyāmakaṃ (syā. ka.);

Ciraṃ tvaṃ anutappesi anutapessasi (sī. pī.), anutappissasi (?), serivāyaṃva vāṇijoti.

If here you should miss the fixed principle of the True Dhamma, long will you grieve, like this merchant Seriva.

Serivavāṇijajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Seriva Merchant Jātaka, the Third.

4. Cūḷaseṭṭhijātakaṃ

4. The Jātaka of the Lesser Treasurer

4.

4.

Appakenapi medhāvī, pābhatena vicakkhaṇo;

Samuṭṭhāpeti attānaṃ, aṇuṃ aggiṃva sandhamanti.

Even with little capital, a wise and discerning person establishes themself, just as one fans a small fire.

Cūḷa culla (sī.), cullaka (syā. pī.) seṭṭhijātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Cūḷaseṭṭhi Jātaka, the Fourth.

5. Taṇḍulanāḷijātakaṃ

5. The Rice-Measure Jātaka

5.

5.

kimagghatī taṇḍulanāḷikā ca, bārāṇasī antarabāhirāni; assapañcasate tāni, ekā taṇḍulanāḷikāti; (syā.) Kimagghati taṇḍulanāḷikāya, assāna mūlāya vadehi rāja nāḷikā ca (sī.), nāḷikāya (ka. sī. aṭṭha.);

Bārāṇasiṃ santarabāhirato bāhirantaṃ (sī.), ayamagghati taṇḍulanāḷikāti kimagghatī vaṇḍulanāḷikā ca, bārāṇasī antarabāhirāni; assapañcasate tāni, ekā taṇḍulanāḷikāti; (syā.).

O King, tell me, what is this measure of rice, the price for the horses, worth? This measure of rice is worth all of Bārāṇasī, including what is inside and out.

Taṇḍulanāḷijātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Taṇḍulanāḷi Jātaka, the Fifth.

6. Devadhammajātakaṃ

6. The Jātaka on the Divine Qualities

6.

6.

Hiriottappasampannā[T 1.0003], sukkadhammasamāhitā;

Santo sappurisā loke, devadhammāti vuccareti.

Endowed with shame and fear of wrongdoing, established in bright qualities, the peaceful, good persons in the world are called 'those with divine qualities'.

Devadhammajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Devadhamma Jātaka, the Sixth.

7. Kaṭṭhahārijātakaṃ

7. The Wood-Carrier Jātaka

7.

7.

Putto tyāhaṃ mahārāja, tvaṃ maṃ posa janādhipa;

Aññepi devo poseti, kiñca kiñci (ka.) devo sakaṃ pajanti.

Great King, I am your son; nourish me, O ruler of men! Your Majesty nourishes even others; why not your own offspring?

Kaṭṭhahāri kaṭṭhavāhana (ka.) jātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Kaṭṭhahāri Jātaka, the Seventh.

8. Gāmaṇijātakaṃ

8. The Jātaka of the Headman

8.

8.

Api [V 1.0003][M 1.0003] ataramānānaṃ, phalāsāva samijjhati;

Vipakkabrahmacariyosmi, evaṃ jānāhi gāmaṇīti.

For those who do not hasten, the desired fruit surely ripens. I am one whose holy life has come to fruition; know this, O headman.

Gāmaṇijātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Gāmaṇi Jātaka, the Eighth.

9. Maghadevajātakaṃ

9. The Maghadeva Jātaka

9.

9.

Uttamaṅgaruhā mayhaṃ, ime jātā vayoharā;

Pātubhūtā devadūtā, pabbajjāsamayo mamāti.

These hairs on my head, bringers of age, have arisen for me; the messengers of Death have appeared. It is the time for my renunciation.

Maghadeva makhādeva (sī. pī.), devadūta (ka.) jātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Maghadeva Jātaka, the Ninth.

10. Sukhavihārijātakaṃ

10. The Jātaka of Dwelling Happily

10.

10.

Yañca [T 1.0004] aññe na rakkhanti, yo ca aññe na rakkhati;

Sa ve rāja sukhaṃ seti, kāmesu anapekkhavāti.

He whom others do not protect, and who does not protect others—that one, O King, indeed sleeps happily, being unconcerned with sensual pleasures.

Sukhavihārijātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Sukhavihāri Jātaka, the Tenth.

Apaṇṇakavaggo paṭhamo.

The Apaṇṇaka Chapter, the First.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Varāpaṇṇaka vaṇṇupatha serivaro, suvicakkhaṇa taṇḍulanāḷikassā;

Hiri puttavaruttagāmaṇinā, yo ca na rakkhati tena dasāti.

The excellent Apaṇṇaka, Vaṇṇupatha, and the noble Seriva; Suvicakkhaṇa and Taṇḍulanāḷika; Hiri, Putta, Varutta, and Gāmaṇi; and 'He Who Protects Not'—with these, there are ten.

2. Sīlavaggo

2. The Chapter on Virtue

11. Lakkhaṇamigajātakaṃ

11. The Lakkhaṇa Deer Jātaka

11.

11.

Hoti sīlavataṃ attho, paṭisanthāra paṭisandhāra (ka.) vuttinaṃ;

Lakkhaṇaṃ passa āyantaṃ, ñātisaṅghapurakkhataṃ purakkhitaṃ (syā.), purekkhitaṃ (ka.);

Atha passasimaṃ kāḷaṃ, suvihīnaṃva ñātibhīti.

There is benefit for the virtuous, for those who practice hospitality. See Lakkhaṇa coming, escorted by his retinue of kinsmen. Then see this Kāḷa, as though completely forsaken by his kin.

Lakkhaṇamigajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Lakkhaṇa Deer Jātaka, the First.

12. Nigrodhamigajātakaṃ

12. The Nigrodha Deer Jātaka

12.

12.

Nigrodhameva [T 1.0005][V 1.0004][M 1.0004] seveyya, na sākhamupasaṃvase;

Nigrodhasmiṃ mataṃ seyyo, yañce sākhasmi sākhasmiṃ (sī. pī.) jīvitanti.

One should associate only with Nigrodha; one should not dwell with Sākha. Better is death under Nigrodha than the life that is with Sākha.

Nigrodhamigajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Nigrodha Deer Jātaka, the Second.

13. Kaṇḍijātakaṃ

13. The Kaṇḍi Jātaka

13.

13.

Dhiratthu kaṇḍinaṃ sallaṃ, purisaṃ gāḷhavedhinaṃ;

Dhiratthu taṃ janapadaṃ, yatthitthī pariṇāyikā;

Te cāpi dhikkitā dhikkatā (?) sattā, ye itthīnaṃ vasaṃgatāti.

Shame on the barbed arrow and the man who pierces deeply! Shame on that country where a woman is the leader! And censured too are those beings who have fallen under the power of women.

Kaṇḍijātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Kaṇḍi Jātaka, the Third.

14. Vātamigajātakaṃ

14. The Vātamiga Jātaka

14.

14.

Na kiratthi rasehi pāpiyo, āvāsehi va vā (sabbattha) santhavehi vā;

Vātamigaṃ gahananissitaṃ gehanissitaṃ (sī. pī.), vasamānesi rasehi sañjayoti.

Surely, nothing is more wicked than tastes—or than dwellings, or friendships. You, Sañjaya, by means of tastes, brought under your power the wind-deer that dwells in the thicket.

Vātamigajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Vātamiga Jātaka, the Fourth.

15. Kharādiyajātakaṃ

15. The Kharādiya Jātaka

15.

15.

Aṭṭhakkhuraṃ kharādiye, migaṃ vaṅkātivaṅkinaṃ;

Sattahi [T 1.0006] kālātikkantaṃ sattahi kalāha’tikkantaṃ (sī.), sattakāleha’tikkantaṃ (syā.), sattahi kālāha’tikkantaṃ (pī.), na naṃ ovaditussaheti.

O Kharādiyā, that eight-hoofed deer, with horns so very crooked, has seven times transgressed the time for admonishment; I am not able to instruct him.

Kharādiyajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Kharādiya Jātaka, the Fifth.

16. Tipallatthamigajātakaṃ

16. The Tipallattha Deer Jātaka

16.

16.

Migaṃ [M 1.0005] tipallattha tipallatta (ka.) manekamāyaṃ, aṭṭhakkhuraṃ aḍḍharattāpapāyiṃ aḍḍharattāvapāyiṃ (sī. pī.);

Ekena sotena chamāssasanto, chahi kalāhitibhoti kalāhatibhoti (sī. syā. pī.) bhāgineyyoti.

O sister, I have taught the deer's cunning to my nephew—the deer who lies in three ways, who has many tricks, who is eight-hoofed, and who drinks after midnight—so that, breathing onto the ground with a single nostril, he might overcome the hunter with his six skills.

Tipallatthamigajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Tipallattha Deer Jātaka, the Sixth.

17. Mālutajātakaṃ

17. The Māluta Jātaka

17.

17.

Kāḷe [V 1.0005] vā yadi vā juṇhe, yadā vāyati māluto;

Vātajāni hi sītāni, ubhotthamaparājitāti.

Whether during the waning moon or the waxing, whenever the wind blows—for cold is born from the wind—in this matter, both are undefeated.

Mālutajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Māluta Jātaka, the Seventh.

18. Matakabhattajātakaṃ

18. The Matakabhatta Jātaka

18.

18.

Evaṃ ce sattā jāneyyuṃ, dukkhāyaṃ jātisambhavo;

Na pāṇo pāṇinaṃ haññe, pāṇaghātī hi socatīti.

If beings were to know thus, that this birth and arising is suffering, a living being would not kill another living being; for the killer of living beings grieves.

Matakabhattajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Matakabhatta Jātaka, the Eighth.

19. Āyācitabhattajātakaṃ

19. The Āyācitabhatta Jātaka

19.

19.

Sace [T 1.0007] mucce muñce (sī. syā. pī.) pecca mucce muñce (sī. syā. pī.), muccamāno hi bajjhati;

Na hevaṃ dhīrā muccanti, mutti bālassa bandhananti.

If one would be free, one should be free in the world to come. For one who is being freed is indeed bound. The wise are not freed in such a way; the freedom of a fool is a bond.

Āyācitabhattajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Āyācitabhatta Jātaka, the Ninth.

20. Naḷapānajātakaṃ

20. The Naḷapāna Jātaka

20.

20.

Disvā padamanuttiṇṇaṃ, disvānotaritaṃ padaṃ;

Naḷena vāriṃ pissāma pivissāma (sī. syā. pī.), neva na ca (ka.) maṃ tvaṃ vadhissasīti.

Seeing no footprint that has come out, but seeing the footprint that has gone down, we shall drink water with a reed; in this way, you will not kill me.

Naḷapānajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Naḷapāna Jātaka, the Tenth.

Sīlavaggo dutiyo.

The Sīla Vagga, the Second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Atha [M 1.0006] lakkhaṇa sākha dhiratthu puna, na kiratthi rasehi kharādiyā;

Atibhoti vara rasa (sabbattha) māluta pāṇa, muccena naḷaavhayanena bhavanti dasāti.

Then Lakkhaṇa, Sākha, and Dhiratthu; again, Vātamiga and Kharādiya; Tipallattha, Māluta, Matakabhatta, Āyācitabhatta, and the one named Naḷa—these are the ten.

3. Kuruṅgavaggo

3. The Kuruṅga Chapter

21. Kuruṅgamigajātakaṃ

21. The Kuruṅgamiga Jātaka

21.

21.

Ñātametaṃ [V 1.0006] kuruṅgassa, yaṃ tvaṃ sepaṇṇi siyyasi seyyasi (sī. syā. pī.);

Aññaṃ [T 1.0008] sepaṇṇi gacchāmi, na me te ruccate phalanti.

This is known to the Kuruṅga deer, O Sepaṇṇi tree, what you are rolling down. I will go to another Sepaṇṇi tree; your fruit does not please me.

Kuruṅgamigajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Kuruṅgamiga Jātaka, the First.

22. Kukkurajātakaṃ

22. The Kukkura Jātaka

22.

22.

Ye kukkurā rājakulamhi vaddhā, koleyyakā vaṇṇabalūpapannā;

Teme na vajjhā mayamasma vajjhā, nāyaṃ saghaccā dubbalaghātikāyanti.

Those dogs raised in the royal household, of noble breed, endowed with beauty and strength—they are not to be killed; it is we who are to be killed. This is not a general slaughter, but a slaughter of the weak.

Kukkurajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Kukkura Jātaka, the Second.

23. Gojānīyajātakaṃ

23. The Gojānīya Jātaka

23.

23.

Api passena semāno, sallebhi sallalīkato;

Seyyova vaḷavā gojo bhojjo (sī.), bhojjho (syā. pī.), yuñja maññeva sārathīti.

Though I lie upon my side, riddled with arrows, a Gojānīya thoroughbred is still better than a common steed. Yoke me and me alone, O charioteer!

Gojānīya bhojājānīya (sī. syā. pī.) jātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Gojānīya Jātaka, the Third.

24. Ājaññajātakaṃ

24. The Ājañña Jātaka

24.

24.

Yadā yadā yattha yadā, yattha yattha yadā yadā;

Ājañño kurute vegaṃ, hāyanti tattha vāḷavāti.

Whenever and wherever a thoroughbred exerts its force, there the common horses fall behind.

Ājaññajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Ājañña Jātaka, the Fourth.

25. Titthajātakaṃ

25. The Tittha Jātaka

25.

25.

Aññamaññehi [T 1.0009][M 1.0007] titthehi, assaṃ pāyehi sārathi;

Accāsanassa puriso, pāyāsassapi tappatīti.

O charioteer, give the horse to drink from different fords. A person who has overeaten is satisfied even with rice-porridge.

Titthajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Tittha Jātaka, the Fifth.

26. Mahiḷāmukhajātakaṃ

26. The Mahiḷāmukha Jātaka

26.

26.

Purāṇacorāna [V 1.0007] vaco nisamma, mahiḷāmukho pothayamanvacārī;

Susaññatānañhi vaco nisamma, gajuttamo sabbaguṇesu aṭṭhāti.

Having heard the words of the thieves of old, Mahiḷāmukha went about striking. Indeed, having heard the words of the well-restrained, the supreme elephant was established in all virtues.

Mahiḷāmukhajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Mahiḷāmukha Jātaka, the Sixth.

27. Abhiṇhajātakaṃ

27. The Abhiṇha Jātaka

27.

27.

Nālaṃ kabaḷaṃ padātave, na ca piṇḍaṃ na kuse na ghaṃsituṃ;

Maññāmi abhiṇhadassanā, nāgo snehamakāsi sinehamakāsi (sī. syā. pī.) kukkureti.

He is not able to take a morsel, nor a lump of food, nor grass, nor to be rubbed down. I think that from constantly seeing it, the elephant has formed an affection for the dog.

Abhiṇhajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Abhiṇha Jātaka, the Seventh.

28. Nandivisālajātakaṃ

28. The Nandivisāla Jātaka

28.

28.

Manuññameva [T 1.0010] bhāseyya, nāmanuññaṃ kudācanaṃ;

Manuññaṃ bhāsamānassa, garuṃ bhāraṃ udaddhari;

Dhanañca naṃ alābhesi, tena cattamano ahūti.

One should speak only what is pleasant; one should never speak what is unpleasant. For the one who spoke pleasantly, he pulled the heavy load. He also caused him to obtain wealth, and by that, the brahmin was pleased.

Nandivisālajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Nandivisāla Jātaka, the Eighth.

29. Kaṇhajātakaṃ

29. The Kaṇha Jātaka

29.

29.

Yato yato garu dhuraṃ, yato gambhīravattanī;

Tadāssu kaṇhaṃ yuñjanti, svāssu taṃ vahate dhuranti.

Wherever the yoke is heavy, wherever the track is deep, then they yoke Kaṇha. He indeed bears that yoke.

Kaṇhajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Kaṇha Jātaka, the Ninth.

30. Munikajātakaṃ

30. The Munika Jātaka

30.

30.

Mā [M 1.0008] munikassa pihayi, āturannāni bhuñjati;

Appossukko bhusaṃ khāda, etaṃ dīghāyulakkhaṇanti.

Do not envy Munika; he eats the food of one who is to be slaughtered. Being free from anxiety, eat chaff. This is the sign of a long life.

Munikajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Munika Jātaka, the Tenth.

Kuruṅgavaggo tatiyo.

The Kuruṅga Chapter, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Kuruṅgassa [V 1.0008] kukkuragojavaro, puna vāḷavassasirivhayano sirivayano (sabbattha);

Mahiḷāmukhanāmanuññavaro, vahate dhura munikena dasāti.

The Kuruṅga Jātaka, the Kukkura and Gojāniya Jātakas, the Ājañña and Tittha Jātakas, the Mahiḷāmukha and Abhiṇha Jātakas, the Nandivisāla, Kaṇha, and Munika Jātakas; these are the ten.

4. Kulāvakavaggo

4. The Kulāvaka Chapter

31. Kulāvakajātakaṃ

4. The Kulāvaka Jātaka

31.

31.

Kulāvakā [T 1.0011] mātali simbalismiṃ, īsāmukhena parivajjayassu;

Kāmaṃ cajāma asuresu pāṇaṃ, mā me dijā vikkulavā māyime dijā vikulāvā (sī. syā. pī.) ahesunti.

31. O Mātali, in the silk-cotton tree there are nestlings; avoid it with the chariot-pole. Willingly, let us give up our lives among the Asuras, but let not these twice-born ones of mine become nestless.

Kulāvakajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Kulāvaka Jātaka, the First.

32. Naccajātakaṃ

The Nacca Jātaka

32.

32.

Rudaṃ manuññaṃ rucirā ca piṭṭhi, veḷuriyavaṇṇūpanibhā vaṇṇūpaṭibhā (syā.), vaṇṇasannibhā (ka.) ca gīvā;

Byāmamattāni ca pekhuṇāni, naccena te dhītaraṃ no dadāmīti.

32. Your cry is pleasant and your back is lovely; your neck is like the color of a beryl gem, and your tail-feathers are a fathom in measure. But because of your dancing, I will not give my daughter to you.

Naccajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Nacca Jātaka, the Second.

33. Sammodamānajātakaṃ

The Sammodamāna Jātaka

33.

33.

Sammodamānā [M 1.0009] gacchanti, jālamādāya pakkhino;

Yadā te vivadissanti, tadā ehinti me vasanti.

33. Living in concord, the birds go, taking the net with them. When they quarrel, then they will come into my power.

Sammodamānajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Sammodamāna Jātaka, the Third.

34. Macchajātakaṃ

The Maccha Jātaka

34.

34.

Na [T 1.0012] maṃ sītaṃ na maṃ uṇhaṃ, na maṃ jālasmi bādhanaṃ;

Yañca maṃ maññate macchī, aññaṃ so ratiyā gatoti.

34. The cold does not afflict me, nor the heat, nor being bound in the net. But that the she-fish thinks of me, ‘He has gone to another for pleasure’—that is what afflicts me.

Macchajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Maccha Jātaka, the Fourth.

35. Vaṭṭakajātakaṃ

35. The Quail Jātaka

35.

35.

Santi [V 1.0009] pakkhā apatanā, santi pādā avañcanā;

Mātāpitā ca nikkhantā, jātaveda paṭikkamāti.

I have wings, but am unable to fly; I have feet, but am unable to walk. My mother and father have departed. O Jātaveda, turn back!

Vaṭṭakajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Quail Jātaka, the Fifth.

36. Sakuṇajātakaṃ

36. The Bird Jātaka

36.

36.

Yaṃ nissitā jagatiruhaṃ vihaṅgamā, svāyaṃ aggiṃ pamuñcati;

Disā bhajatha vakkaṅgā vaṅkaṅgā (syā.), jātaṃ saraṇato bhayanti.

That very tree upon which we birds depend now emits fire. Flee to all directions, O flock of birds! Fear has arisen from our refuge.

Sakuṇajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Bird Jātaka, the Sixth.

37. Tittirajātakaṃ

37. The Partridge Jātaka

37.

37.

Ye vuḍḍha vaddha (sī. pī.) mapacāyanti, narā dhammassa kovidā;

Diṭṭheva dhamme pāsaṃsā, samparāye ca suggatīti.

Those people who honor their elders, being skilled in the Dhamma, are praised in this very life and attain a good destination in the next.

Tittirajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Partridge Jātaka, the Seventh.

38. Bakajātakaṃ

38. The Heron Jātaka

38.

38.

Nāccantaṃ [T 1.0013] nikatippañño, nikatyā sukhamedhati;

Ārādheti nikatippañño ārādhe nikatippañño (pī.), bako kakkaṭakāmivāti.

One who is excessively deceitful does not prosper in happiness through deceit; the deceitful one reaps an evil result, just as the heron did from the crab.

Bakajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Heron Jātaka, the Eighth.

39. Nandajātakaṃ

39. The Nanda Jātaka

39.

39.

Maññe [M 1.0010] sovaṇṇayo rāsi, soṇṇamālā ca nandako;

Yattha dāso āmajāto, ṭhito thullāni thūlāni (ka.) gajjatīti.

I think that where the home-born slave Nandaka stands and roars coarse words, there is a heap of gold and a golden garland.

Nandajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Nanda Jātaka, the Ninth.

40. Khadiraṅgārajātakaṃ

40. The Acacia-Charcoal Jātaka

40.

40.

Kāmaṃ [V 1.0010] patāmi nirayaṃ, uddhaṃpādo avaṃsiro;

Nānariyaṃ karissāmi, handa piṇḍaṃ paṭiggahāti.

Willingly would I fall into hell, feet up and head down, yet I will not do an ignoble deed. Come, please accept this almsfood.

Khadiraṅgārajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Khadiraṅgāra Jātaka, the Tenth.

Kulāvakavaggo catuttho.

The Kulāvaka Chapter, the Fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sirimātali dhītara pakkhivaro, ratiyāgato mātāpitā ca puna;

Jagatīruha vuḍḍha sukakkaṭako, tathā nandakapiṇḍavarena dasāti.

Siri, Mātali, the Daughter, the Best of Birds; the one Gone for Pleasure, and Mother and Father; the Tree, the Elder, the Good Crab; and Nanda with the Excellent Almsfood make ten.

5. Atthakāmavaggo

5. The Chapter on Desiring Welfare

41. Losakajātakaṃ

41. The Losaka Jātaka

41.

41.

Yo [T 1.0014] atthakāmassa hitānukampino, ovajjamāno na karoti sāsanaṃ;

Ajiyā pādamolamba pādamolumba (sī. syā. pī.), mittako viya socatīti.

Whoever, being admonished, does not follow the instruction of a compassionate well-wisher, grieves like Mittaka hanging on to the foot of a she-goat.

Losakajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Losaka Jātaka, the First.

42. Kapotajātakaṃ

42. The Pigeon Jātaka

42.

42.

Yo [M 1.0011] atthakāmassa hitānukampino, ovajjamāno na karoti sāsanaṃ;

Kapotakassa vacanaṃ akatvā, amittahatthatthagatova setīti.

Whoever, being admonished, does not follow the instruction of a compassionate well-wisher, not having followed the word of the pigeon, lies fallen into the hands of an enemy.

Kapotajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Pigeon Jātaka, the Second.

43. Veḷukajātakaṃ

43. The Bamboo Jātaka

43.

43.

Yo atthakāmassa hitānukampino, ovajjamāno na karoti sāsanaṃ;

Evaṃ so nihato seti, veḷukassa yathā pitāti.

Whoever, being admonished, does not follow the instruction of a compassionate well-wisher, lies slain just so, like the father of Veḷuka.

Veḷukajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Bamboo Jātaka, the Third.

44. Makasajātakaṃ

44. The Mosquito Jātaka

44.

44.

Seyyo [T 1.0015][V 1.0011] amitto matiyā upeto, na tveva mitto mativippahīno;

Makasaṃ vadhissanti hi eḷamūgo, putto pitu abbhidā uttamaṅganti.

Better an enemy endowed with intelligence than a friend devoid of wisdom. Thinking, 'I will kill the mosquito,' the foolish, drooling son split his father's head.

Makasajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Mosquito Jātaka, the Fourth.

45. Rohiṇijātakaṃ

45. The Rohiṇī Jātaka

45.

45.

Seyyo amitto medhāvī, yañce bālānukampako;

Passa rohiṇikaṃ jammiṃ, mātaraṃ hantvāna socatīti.

Better a wise enemy than a foolish sympathizer. Behold the wretched Rohiṇī, who grieves after having killed her own mother.

Rohiṇijātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Rohiṇī Jātaka, the Fifth.

46. Ārāmadūsakajātakaṃ

46. The Garden-Despoiler Jātaka

46.

46.

Na ve anatthakusalena, atthacariyā sukhāvahā;

Hāpeti atthaṃ dummedho, kapi ārāmiko yathāti.

For one unskilled in what is beneficial, the practice of what is beneficial does not bring happiness; the person of little wisdom ruins the goal, just as the monkey gardener did.

Ārāmadūsakajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Garden-Despoiler Jātaka, the Sixth.

47. Vāruṇidūsakajātakaṃ

47. The Liquor-Spoiling Jātaka

47.

47.

Na [M 1.0012] ve anatthakusalena, atthacariyā sukhāvahā;

Hāpeti atthaṃ dummedho, koṇḍañño vāruṇiṃ yathāti.

Truly, for one unskilled in what is beneficial, the practice of what is beneficial does not bring happiness; the person of little wisdom ruins the goal, just as Koṇḍañña did with the liquor.

Vāruṇidūsakajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Vāruṇidūsaka Jātaka, the Seventh.

48. Vedabbajātakaṃ

48. The Vedabba Jātaka

48.

48.

Anupāyena [T 1.0016] yo atthaṃ, icchati so vihaññati;

Cetā haniṃsu vedabbaṃ vedabbhaṃ (sī. pī.), sabbe te byasanamajjhagūti.

Whoever seeks a goal by improper means is vexed; the men of Ceta killed Vedabba, and they all met with disaster.

Vedabba vedabbha (sī. pī.) jātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Vedabba Jātaka, the Eighth.

49. Nakkhattajātakaṃ

49. The Nakkhatta Jātaka

49.

49.

Nakkhattaṃ [V 1.0012] paṭimānentaṃ, attho bālaṃ upaccagā;

Attho atthassa nakkhattaṃ, kiṃ karissanti tārakāti.

While the fool was waiting for the constellation, his purpose passed him by. The purpose itself is the constellation of that purpose; what can the stars do?

Nakkhattajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Nakkhatta Jātaka, the Ninth.

50. Dummedhajātakaṃ

50. The Dummedha Jātaka

50.

50.

Dummedhānaṃ sahassena, yañño me upayācito;

Idāni khohaṃ yajissāmi, bahu bahū (sī. pī.), bahuṃ (ka.) adhammiko janoti.

A sacrifice with a thousand fools has been vowed by me. Now indeed I shall perform the sacrifice, for many people are unrighteous.

Dummedhajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Dummedha Jātaka, the Tenth.

Atthakāmavaggo pañcamo.

The Chapter on Desiring Benefit, the Fifth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Atha mittaka mātu kapotavaro, tathā veḷūka eḷamūgo rohiṇī;

Kapi [T 1.0017] vāruṇi cetacarā ca puna, tathā tāraka yaññavarena dasāti.

Then Losaka and the excellent Kapota; also Veḷuka, Eḷamūga (Makasa), and Rohiṇī; Kapi (Ārāmadūsaka), Vāruṇi (Vāruṇidūsaka), and Cetacarā (Vedabba); and again, Tāraka (Nakkhatta) and the excellent Yañña (Dummedha) make ten.

Paṭhamo paṇṇāsako.

The First Fifty.

6. Āsīsavaggo

6. The Chapter on Aspiration

51.Mahāsīlavajātakaṃ

51. The Mahāsīlava Jātaka

51.

51.

Āsīsetheva [M 1.0013] āsiṃsetheva (sī. syā. pī.) puriso, na nibbindeyya paṇḍito;

Passāmi vohaṃ attānaṃ, yathā icchiṃ tathā ahūti.

A person should indeed maintain aspiration; a wise one should not become disheartened. I see myself: just as I wished, so it has come to be.

Mahāsīlavajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Mahāsīlava Jātaka, the First.

52. Cūḷajanakajātakaṃ

52. The Cūḷajanaka Jātaka

52.

52.

Vāyametheva puriso, na nibbindeyya paṇḍito;

Passāmi vohaṃ attānaṃ, udakā thalamubbhatanti.

A person should indeed strive; a wise one should not become weary. I see myself, lifted from the water onto dry land.

Cūḷajanakajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Cūḷajanaka Jātaka, the Second.

53. Puṇṇapātijātakaṃ

53. The Puṇṇapāti Jātaka

53.

53.

Tatheva [V 1.0013] puṇṇā pātiyo, aññāyaṃ vattate kathā;

Ākāraṇena ākārakena (sī. syā. pī.) jānāmi, na cāyaṃ bhaddikā surāti.

The bowls are full just as before, yet this report is different. For this reason, I know for certain this is not fine liquor.

Puṇṇapātijātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Puṇṇapāti Jātaka, the Third.

54. Kiṃphalajātakaṃ

54. The Kiṃphala Jātaka

54.

54.

Nāyaṃ [T 1.0018] rukkho durāruho, napi gāmato ārakā;

Ākāraṇena jānāmi, nāyaṃ sāduphalo dumoti.

This tree is not difficult to climb, nor is it far from the village; for this reason, I know this is not a tree with sweet fruit.

Kiṃphalajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Kiṃphala Jātaka, the Fourth.

55. Pañcāvudhajātakaṃ

55. The Pañcāvudha Jātaka

55.

55.

Yo alīnena cittena, alīnamanaso naro;

Bhāveti kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, yogakkhemassa pattiyā;

Pāpuṇe anupubbena, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayanti.

The person who, with an unsluggish mind and unsluggish heart, develops the wholesome Dhamma for the attainment of security from bondage, will gradually attain the destruction of all fetters.

Pañcāvudhajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Pañcāvudha Jātaka, the Fifth.

56. Kañcanakkhandhajātakaṃ

56. The Kañcanakkhandha Jātaka

56.

56.

Yo [M 1.0014] pahaṭṭhena cittena, pahaṭṭhamanaso naro;

Bhāveti kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, yogakkhemassa pattiyā;

Pāpuṇe anupubbena, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayanti.

The person who, with a gladdened mind and gladdened heart, develops the wholesome Dhamma for the attainment of security from bondage, will gradually attain the destruction of all fetters.

Kañcanakkhandhajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Kañcanakkhandha Jātaka, the Sixth.

57. Vānarindajātakaṃ

57. The Vānarinda Jātaka

57.

57.

Yassete caturo dhammā, vānarinda yathā tava;

Saccaṃ dhammo dhiti dhitī (sī. pī.) cāgo, diṭṭhaṃ so ativattatīti.

O monkey king, one in whom are found these four qualities, just as they are in you—truth, wisdom, fortitude, and relinquishment—overcomes their enemy.

Vānarindajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Vānarinda Jātaka, the Seventh.

58. Tayodhammajātakaṃ

58. The Tayodhamma Jātaka

58.

58.

Yassete [T 1.0019][V 1.0014] ca yassa ete (sī. pī.) tayo dhammā, vānarinda yathā tava;

Dakkhiyaṃ sūriyaṃ paññā, diṭṭhaṃ so ativattatīti.

O monkey king, one in whom are found these three qualities, just as they are in you—dexterity, heroism, and wisdom—overcomes their enemy.

Tayodhammajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Tayodhamma Jātaka, the Eighth.

59. Bherivādakajātakaṃ

59. The Bherivādaka Jātaka

59.

59.

Dhame dhame nātidhame, atidhantañhi pāpakaṃ;

Dhantena hi sataṃ laddhaṃ, atidhantena nāsitanti.

Beat, beat, but do not over-beat; for excessive beating is indeed wicked. By beating, a hundred were gained; by excessive beating, they were lost.

Bherivādakajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Bherivādaka Jātaka, the Ninth.

60. Saṅkhadhamajātakaṃ

60. The Saṅkhadhama Jātaka

60.

60.

Dhame dhame nātidhame, atidhantañhi pāpakaṃ;

Dhantenādhigatā bhogā, te tāto vidhamī dhamanti.

Blow, blow, but do not over-blow; for excessive blowing is indeed wicked. By blowing, wealth was acquired; O father, by your constant blowing, you destroy it.

Saṅkhadhamajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Saṅkhadhama Jātaka, the Tenth.

Āsīsavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Chapter on Aspiration, the Sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Yathā [M 1.0015] icchiṃ tathāhudakā thalā, sura sāduphalo ca alīnamano;

Sampahaṭṭhamano [T 1.0020] caturo ca tayo, sataladdhaka bhogadhanena dasāti.

‘As I wished,’ ‘from water to land,’ ‘liquor,’ ‘sweet fruit,’ ‘unsluggish mind,’ ‘gladdened mind,’ ‘four,’ ‘three,’ ‘gaining a hundred,’ and ‘wealth’ make ten.

7. Itthivaggo

7. The Chapter on Women

61. Asātamantajātakaṃ

61. The Asātamanta Jātaka

61.

61.

Asā lokitthiyo nāma, velā tāsaṃ na vijjati;

Sārattā ca pagabbhā ca, sikhī sabbaghaso yathā;

Tā hitvā pabbajissāmi, vivekamanubrūhayanti.

In this world, women are indeed base; for them, no limit is found. They are passionate and audacious, like an all-consuming fire. Having abandoned them, I will go forth and cultivate seclusion.

Asātamantajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Asātamanta Jātaka, the First.

62. Aṇḍabhūtajātakaṃ

62. The Aṇḍabhūta Jātaka

62.

62.

Yaṃ [V 1.0015] brāhmaṇo avādesi, vīṇaṃ samukhaveṭhito;

Aṇḍabhūtā bhatā bhariyā, tāsu ko jātu vissaseti.

The brahmin played the lute, wrapped in its covering. A wife is brought up as if from an egg; who, then, could ever place trust in them?

Aṇḍabhūtajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Aṇḍabhūta Jātaka, the Second.

63. Takkapaṇḍitajātakaṃ

63. The Takka Paṇḍita Jātaka

63.

63.

Kodhanā akataññū ca, pisuṇā mittabhedikā pisuṇā ca vibhedikā (sī. syā. pī.);

Brahmacariyaṃ cara bhikkhu, so sukhaṃ na vihāhasīti pihāhisīti (sī. syā. pī.), vihāyasi (ka.).

They are angry and ungrateful, slanderous and breakers of friendships. O bhikkhu, live the holy life; thus you will not fall away from happiness.

Takkapaṇḍitajātakaṃ takkajātakaṃ (sī. syā. pī. aṭṭha.) tatiyaṃ.

The Takka Paṇḍita Jātaka, the Third.

64. Durājānajātakaṃ

64. The Durājāna Jātaka

64.

64.

Mā [T 1.0021] su nandi icchati maṃ, mā su soci na micchati na icchati (sī. syā. pī.);

Thīnaṃ bhāvo durājāno, macchassevodake gatanti.

Do not rejoice, thinking, ‘She wants me’; do not grieve, thinking, ‘She does not want me.’ The nature of women is hard to know, like the path of a fish in the water.

Durājānajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Durājāna Jātaka, the Fourth.

65. Anabhiratijātakaṃ

65. The Anabhirati Jātaka

65.

65.

Yathā [M 1.0016] nadī ca pantho ca, pānāgāraṃ sabhā papā;

Evaṃ lokitthiyo nāma, nāsaṃ kujjhanti paṇḍitāti.

Like a river and a road, a tavern, an assembly hall, and a public watering place, so in this world are women common to all; the wise do not get angry with them.

Anabhiratijātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Anabhirati Jātaka, the Fifth.

66. Mudulakkhaṇajātakaṃ

66. The Mudulakkhaṇā Jātaka

66.

66.

Ekā icchā pure āsi, aladdhā mudulakkhaṇaṃ;

Yato laddhā aḷārakkhī, icchā icchaṃ vijāyathāti.

Formerly, before obtaining Mudulakkhaṇā, I had but one desire. But since I have obtained the large-eyed one, desire gives birth to further desire.

Mudulakkhaṇajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Mudulakkhaṇā Jātaka, the Sixth.

67. Ucchaṅgajātakaṃ

67. The Ucchaṅga Jātaka

67.

67.

Ucchaṅge deva me putto, pathe dhāvantiyā pati;

Tañca desaṃ na passāmi, yato sodariyamānayeti sodariyaṃ naye (ka.).

O king, my son is in my lap; a husband is on the path for a woman who travels. But I do not see that country from which I could bring a brother.

Ucchaṅgajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Ucchaṅga Jātaka, the Seventh.

68. Sāketajātakaṃ

68. The Sāketa Jātaka

68.

68.

Yasmiṃ [T 1.0022][V 1.0016] mano nivisati, cittañcāpi cittaṃ vāpi (katthaci) pasīdati;

Adiṭṭhapubbake pose, kāmaṃ tasmimpi vissaseti.

In whom the mind settles and the heart becomes serene, one may readily place trust even in a person never seen before.

Sāketajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Sāketa Jātaka, the Eighth.

69. Visavantajātakaṃ

69. The Visavanta Jātaka

69.

69.

Dhiratthu taṃ visaṃ vantaṃ, yamahaṃ jīvitakāraṇā;

Vantaṃ paccāvamissāmi paccāharissāmi (ka.), mataṃ me jīvitā varanti.

Fie on that poison I vomited! That I, for the sake of my life, should swallow again what was vomited—death is better for me than life!

Visavantajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Visavanta Jātaka, the Ninth.

70. Kuddālajātakaṃ

70. The Spade Jātaka

70.

70.

Na taṃ jitaṃ sādhu jitaṃ, yaṃ jitaṃ avajīyati;

Taṃ kho jitaṃ sādhu jitaṃ, yaṃ jitaṃ nāvajīyatīti.

That victory is not well won which can be lost again; that victory is well won which cannot be lost again.

Kuddālajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Kuddāla Jātaka, the tenth.

Itthivaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on Women, the Seventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sikhīsabbaghasopi [M 1.0017] ca vīṇavaro, pisuṇā mittabhedikā nandī nadī;

Mudulakkhaṇa sodariyā ca mano, visa sādhujitena bhavanti dasāti.

The Asātamanta, the Aṇḍabhūta, the Takkapaṇḍita, the Durājāna, the Anabhirati, the Mudulakkhaṇa and the Ucchaṅga, the Sāketa, the Visavanta, together with the Kuddāla—these are the ten.

8. Varuṇavaggo

8. The Varuṇa Chapter

71. Varuṇajātakaṃ

71. The Varuṇa Jātaka

71.

71.

Yo [T 1.0023] pubbe karaṇīyāni, pacchā so kātumicchati;

Varuṇakaṭṭha varaṇakaṭṭha (sī. pī.) bhañjova, sa pacchā manutappatīti.

He who wishes to do later what should be done before, like the youth who broke the varuṇa firewood, later comes to regret it.

Varuṇajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Varuṇa Jātaka, the first.

72. Sīlavahatthijātakaṃ

72. The Jātaka of the Virtuous Elephant

72.

72.

Akataññussa [V 1.0017] posassa, niccaṃ vivaradassino;

Sabbaṃ ce pathaviṃ paṭhaviṃ (sī. syā. pī.) dajjā, neva naṃ abhirādhayeti.

For an ungrateful person who is always looking for faults, even if one were to give him the entire earth, one could never satisfy him.

Sīlavahatthijātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Jātaka of the Virtuous Elephant, the second.

73. Saccaṃkirajātakaṃ

73. The Saccaṃkira Jātaka

73.

73.

Saccaṃ kirevamāhaṃsu, narā ekacciyā idha;

Kaṭṭhaṃ niplavitaṃ viplāvitaṃ (sī. pī.) seyyo, na tvevekacciyo naroti.

Truly, they say, some wise people here have spoken thus: ‘A salvaged log is better, but never a certain kind of person.’

Saccaṃkirajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Saccaṃkira Jātaka, the third.

74. Rukkhadhammajātakaṃ

74. The Jātaka on the Nature of Trees

74.

74.

Sādhū sambahulā ñātī, api rukkhā araññajā;

Vāto [T 1.0024] vahati ekaṭṭhaṃ, brahantampi vanappatinti.

Many kinsmen are good; so too are many trees born in the forest. The wind can overthrow even a mighty tree if it stands alone.

Rukkhadhammajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Jātaka on the Nature of Trees, the fourth.

75. Macchajātakaṃ

75. The Fish Jātaka

75.

75.

Abhitthanaya [M 1.0018] pajjunna, nidhiṃ kākassa nāsaya;

Kākaṃ sokāya randhehi, mañca sokā pamocayāti.

Thunder, O Pajjunna! Destroy the crow’s treasure! Afflict the crow with sorrow, and from sorrow release me!

Macchajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Fish Jātaka, the fifth.

76. Asaṅkiyajātakaṃ

76. The Asaṅkiya Jātaka

76.

76.

Asaṅkiyomhi gāmamhi, araññe natthi me bhayaṃ;

Ujuṃ maggaṃ samārūḷho, mettāya karuṇāya cāti.

I am free from suspicion in the village; in the forest I have no fear. I have embarked upon the straight path with loving-kindness and compassion.

Asaṅkiyajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Asaṅkiya Jātaka, the sixth.

77. Mahāsupinajātakaṃ

77. The Jātaka of the Great Dreams

77.

77.

Usabhā [V 1.0018] rukkhā gāviyo gavā ca, asso kaṃso siṅgālī sigāsī (sī. syā. pī.) ca kumbho;

Pokkharaṇī ca apākacandanaṃ, lābūni sīdanti silā plavanti.

Bulls, trees, cows and oxen, a horse, a bowl, a she-jackal, and a pot; a lotus pond, uncooked rice and sandalwood; gourds sink and stones float.

Maṇḍūkiyo kaṇhasappe gilanti, kākaṃ supaṇṇā parivārayanti;

Tasā [T 1.0025] vakā eḷakānaṃ bhayāhi, vipariyāso vipariyāyo (syā. ka.) vattati nayidha matthīti.

She-frogs swallow black cobras; garuḍas attend upon a crow; fearsome wolves are frightened by goats. A reversal is taking place; its fulfillment is not here.

Mahāsupinajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Jātaka of the Great Dreams, the seventh.

78. Illisajātakaṃ

78. The Illisa Jātaka

78.

78.

Ubho khañjā ubho kuṇī, ubho visamacakkhukā cakkhulā (sī. pī.);

Ubhinnaṃ piḷakā pīḷakā (syā.) jātā, nāhaṃ passāmi illisanti.

Both are lame, both are crippled, both are squint-eyed; boils have appeared on both of them. I do not recognize Illisa.

Illisajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Illisa Jātaka, the eighth.

79. Kharassarajātakaṃ

79. The Kharassara Jātaka

79.

79.

Yato [M 1.0019] viluttā ca hatā ca gāvo, daḍḍhāni gehāni jano ca nīto;

Athāgamā puttahatāya putto, kharassaraṃ ḍiṇḍimaṃ deṇḍimaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), ḍindimaṃ (ka.) vādayantoti.

When the cattle have been plundered and killed, the houses have been burned, and the people have been led away, then the son of a woman whose son was slain comes, beating a harsh-sounding great drum.

Kharassarajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Kharassara Jātaka, the ninth.

80. Bhīmasenajātakaṃ

80. The Bhīmasena Jātaka

80.

80.

Yaṃ te pavikatthitaṃ pure, atha te pūtisarā sajanti pacchā;

Ubhayaṃ [T 1.0026] na sameti bhīmasena, yuddhakathā ca idañca te vihaññanti.

O Bhīmasena, what you boasted of before, and how excrement and urine now flow from you afterwards—these two do not match: your talk of battle and this affliction of yours.

Bhīmasenajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Bhīmasena Jātaka, the tenth.

Varuṇavaggo varaṇavaggo (sī. pī.) aṭṭhamo.

The Varuṇa Chapter, the eighth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Varuṇā akataññūvare tu saccavaraṃ, savanappatinā ca abhitthanaya;

Karuṇāya silāplava illisato, puna ḍiṇḍimapūtisarena dasāti.

Varuṇa, the excellent ungrateful one, the excellent truth, with the lord of the forest, and ‘Thunder!’; with compassion, the floating stone, from Illisa, again the drum and the foul flow—these are the ten.

9. Apāyimhavaggo

9. The Apāyimha Chapter

81. Surāpānajātakaṃ

81. The Jātaka on Drinking Liquor

81.

81.

Apāyimha [V 1.0019] anaccimha, agāyimha rudimha ca;

Visaññikaraṇiṃ pitvā pītvā (sī. syā. pī.), diṭṭhā nāhumha vānarāti.

We drank, we danced, we sang, and we wept. Having drunk that which causes loss of perception, we were not the monkeys that were seen.

Surāpānajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Jātaka on Drinking Liquor, the first.

82. Mittavindakajātakaṃ

82. The Mittavindaka Jātaka

82.

82.

Atikkamma [T 1.0027][M 1.0020] ramaṇakaṃ, sadāmattañca dūbhakaṃ;

Svāsi pāsāṇamāsīno, yasmā jīvaṃ na mokkhasīti.

Having passed by the crystal palace, the silver palace, and the ruby palace, you have come to the razor-wheel, from which you will not be freed while you live.

Mittavindakajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Mittavindaka Jātaka, the second.

83. Kālakaṇṇijātakaṃ

83. The Kālakaṇṇī Jātaka

83.

83.

Mitto have sattapadena hoti, sahāyo pana dvādasakena hoti;

Māsaḍḍhamāsena ca ñāti hoti, tatuttariṃ attasamopi hoti;

Sohaṃ kathaṃ attasukhassa hetu, cirasanthutaṃ cirasandhavaṃ (ka.), cirasatthunaṃ (pī.) kāḷakaṇṇiṃ jaheyyanti.

Indeed, one becomes a friend by taking seven steps together; a companion, by living together for twelve days. In a month and a half, one becomes a kinsman; and longer than that, one becomes like oneself. How then, for the sake of my own welfare and happiness, could I abandon Kālakaṇṇī, with whom I have been so long familiar?

Kālakaṇṇijātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Kālakaṇṇī Jātaka, the third.

84. Atthassadvārajātakaṃ

84. The Jātaka on the Gates of Welfare

84.

84.

Ārogyamicche paramañca lābhaṃ, sīlañca vuddhānumataṃ sutañca;

Dhammānuvattī ca alīnatā ca, atthassa dvārā pamukhā chaḷeteti.

My dear, one should wish for health, and for supreme gain, and for virtue approved by the wise, and for learning, and for practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, and for diligence. These six are the principal gates of welfare.

Atthassadvārajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Jātaka on the Gates of Welfare, the fourth.

85. Kiṃpakkajātakaṃ

85. The Kimpakka Jātaka

85.

85.

Āyatiṃ [T 1.0028] dosaṃ nāññāya, yo kāme paṭisevati;

Vipākante hananti naṃ, kiṃpakkamiva bhakkhitanti.

Not discerning the future danger, whoever indulges in sensual pleasures is destroyed by them when they ripen, like the eaten kiṃpakka fruit.

Kiṃpakkajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Kimpakka Jātaka, the fifth.

86. Sīlavīmaṃsakajātakaṃ

86. The Sīlavīmaṃsaka Jātaka

86.

86.

Sīlaṃ [V 1.0020] kireva kalyāṇaṃ, sīlaṃ loke anuttaraṃ;

Passa ghoraviso nāgo, sīlavāti na haññatīti.

O great king, it is said that virtue alone is excellent; virtue is unsurpassed in the world. Behold, a serpent of dreadful venom is not killed on the grounds that 'he is virtuous'.

Sīlavīmaṃsakajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Sīlavīmaṃsaka Jātaka, the sixth.

87. Maṅgalajātakaṃ

87. The Maṅgala Jātaka

87.

87.

Yassa [M 1.0021] maṅgalā samūhatāse samūhatā (sī. syā. pī. su. ni. 362, uppātā uppādā (pī.) supinā ca lakkhaṇā ca;

So sa (sī. pī. ka.) maṅgaladosavītivatto, yugayogādhigato na jātumetīti.

O brahmin, for whom auspicious signs, omens, dreams, and marks are uprooted; he, having overcome the fault of signs and transcended the yokes, will never come to be again.

Maṅgalajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Maṅgala Jātaka, the seventh.

88. Sārambhajātakaṃ

88. The Sārambha Jātaka

88.

88.

Kalyāṇimeva muñceyya, na hi muñceyya pāpikaṃ;

Mokkho kalyāṇiyā sādhu, mutvā tappati pāpikanti.

One should speak only what is wholesome; one should not speak what is evil. The speaking of what is wholesome is good; having spoken what is evil, one is tormented.

Sārambhajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Sārambha Jātaka, the eighth.

89. Kuhakajātakaṃ

89. The Kuhaka Jātaka

89.

89.

Vācāva [T 1.0029] kira te āsi, saṇhā sakhilabhāṇino;

Tiṇamatte asajjittho, no ca nikkhasataṃ haranti.

O you of friendly words, your speech was indeed gentle. You were unattached to a mere blade of grass, but not so while stealing a hundred nikkhas.

Kuhakajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Kuhaka Jātaka, the ninth.

90. Akataññujātakaṃ

90. The Akataññu Jātaka

90.

90.

Yo pubbe katakalyāṇo, katattho nāvabujjhati;

Pacchā kicce samuppanne, kattāraṃ nādhigacchatīti.

He who has a good deed done for him before but does not acknowledge his benefactor, will not find anyone to help him when a need arises later.

Akataññujātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Akataññu Jātaka, the tenth.

Apāyimhavaggo navamo.

The Apāyimha Chapter, the ninth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse thereof:

Apāyimha ca dūbhakaṃ sattapadaṃ, chaḷadvara ca āyatinā ca puna;

Ahisīlava maṅgali pāpikassā, sataṃnikkha katatthavarena dasāti.

Apāyimha, Dūbhaka, Sattapada, Chaḷadvara, and again Āyatinā; Ahisīlava, Maṅgali, Pāpikassā, Sataṃnikkha, and Katatthavara make ten.

10. Littavaggo

10. The Litta Chapter

91. Littajātakaṃ

91. The Litta Jātaka

91.

91.

Littaṃ [V 1.0021][M 1.0022] paramena tejasā, gilamakkhaṃ [T 1.0030] puriso na bujjhati;

Gila re gila pāpadhuttaka, pacchā te kaṭukaṃ bhavissatīti.

A man swallowing a die smeared with a potent poison does not realize it. Swallow, O swallow, you wicked gambler! Afterwards it will be bitter for you.

Littajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Litta Jātaka, the first.

92. Mahāsārajātakaṃ

92. The Mahāsāra Jātaka

92.

92.

Ukkaṭṭhe sūramicchanti, mantīsu akutūhalaṃ;

Piyañca annapānamhi, atthe jāte ca paṇḍitanti.

In battle, they want a hero; in counsel, one who is discreet; a pleasant person at food and drink; and a wise man when a matter has arisen.

Mahāsārajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Mahāsāra Jātaka, the second.

93. Visāsabhojanajātakaṃ

93. The Vissāsabhojana Jātaka

93.

93.

Na vissase avissatthe, vissatthepi na vissase;

Vissāsā bhayamanveti, sīhaṃva migamātukāti migamātuyā (ka.).

Do not trust the untrusted, nor place trust in the trusted. From trust, fear arises, just as it did for the lion from the doe.

Visāsabhojanajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Vissāsabhojana Jātaka, the Third.

94. Lomahaṃsajātakaṃ

94. The Lomahaṃsa Jātaka

94.

94.

Sotatto sosindo sosīto (sī. syā. pī.), sosino (ka.) ceva, eko bhiṃsanake vane;

Naggo na caggimāsīno, esanāpasuto munīti.

Scorched by heat and drenched by cold, alone in a frightful forest; naked and not sitting by a fire, the sage is intent on his quest.

Lomahaṃsajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Lomahaṃsa Jātaka, the Fourth.

95. Mahāsudassanajātakaṃ

95. The Mahāsudassana Jātaka

95.

95.

Aniccā [T 1.0031] vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukhoti.

Impermanent, indeed, are conditioned things, subject to arising and passing away. Having arisen, they cease; their pacification is bliss.

Mahāsudassanajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Mahāsudassana Jātaka, the Fifth.

96. Telapattajātakaṃ

96. The Telapatta Jātaka

96.

96.

Samatittikaṃ [V 1.0022] anavasekaṃ, telapattaṃ yathā parihareyya;

Evaṃ sacittamanurakkhe, patthayāno disaṃ agatapubbanti.

Just as one would carry a bowl of oil, filled level with the brim and not to be spilled, so too should one who aspires for the direction not gone to before guard one's own mind.

Telapattajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Telapatta Jātaka, the Sixth.

97. Nāmasiddhijātakaṃ

97. The Nāmasiddhi Jātaka

97.

97.

Jīvakañca [M 1.0023] mataṃ disvā, dhanapāliñca duggataṃ;

Panthakañca vane mūḷhaṃ, pāpako punarāgatoti.

Having seen Jīvaka dead, Dhanapālī destitute, and Panthaka lost in the forest, Pāpaka has returned.

Nāmasiddhijātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Nāmasiddhi Jātaka, the Seventh.

98. Kūṭavāṇijajātakaṃ

98. The Kūṭavāṇija Jātaka

98.

98.

Sādhu [T 1.0032] kho paṇḍito nāma, na tveva atipaṇḍito;

Atipaṇḍitena puttena, manamhi upakūḷitoti upakūlitoti (sī.), upakuṭṭhitoti (syā.), upakuṭito (ka.).

Indeed, a wise person is good, but not one who is over-wise. Because of my son, Atipaṇḍita, my mind is scorched.

Kūṭavāṇijajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Kūṭavāṇija Jātaka, the Eighth.

99. Parosahassajātakaṃ

99. The Parosahassa Jātaka

99.

99.

Parosahassampi samāgatānaṃ, kandeyyuṃ te vassasataṃ apaññā;

Ekova seyyo puriso sapañño, yo bhāsitassa vijānāti atthanti.

Though more than a thousand without wisdom might gather and weep for a hundred years, better is that one wise person who understands the meaning of what has been said.

Parosahassajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Parosahassa Jātaka, the Ninth.

100. Asātarūpajātakaṃ

100. The Asātarūpa Jātaka

100.

100.

Asātaṃ sātarūpena, piyarūpena appiyaṃ;

Dukkhaṃ sukhassa rūpena, pamattamativattatīti.

The disagreeable in the guise of the agreeable, the unloved in the guise of the beloved, and suffering in the guise of happiness, overcome the one who is heedless.

Asātarūpajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Asātarūpa Jātaka, the Tenth.

Littavaggo dasamo.

The Litta Chapter, the Tenth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Gilamakkhakutūhala [T 1.0033][V 1.0023] mātukassā, muninā ca aniccata pattavaraṃ;

Dhanapālivaro atipaṇḍitako, saparosahassaasātadasāti.

Litta, Mahāsāra, Vissāsabhojana, and Lomahaṃsa, Mahāsudassana and the excellent Telapatta; Nāmasiddhi, Kūṭavāṇija, Parosahassa together with Asātarūpa—these are the ten.

Majjhimo paṇṇāsako.

The Middle Fifty.

11. Parosatavaggo

11. The Parosata Chapter

101. Parosatajātakaṃ

101. The Parosata Jātaka

101.

101.

Parosataṃ [M 1.0024] cepi samāgatānaṃ, jhāyeyyuṃ te vassasataṃ apaññā;

Ekova seyyo puriso sapañño, yo bhāsitassa vijānāti atthanti.

Though more than a hundred without wisdom might gather and meditate for a hundred years, better is that one wise person who understands the meaning of what has been said.

Parosatajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Parosata Jātaka, the First.

102. Paṇṇikajātakaṃ

102. The Paṇṇika Jātaka

102.

102.

Yo dukkhaphuṭṭhāya bhaveyya tāṇaṃ, so me pitā dubbhi dūbhi (sī. pī.) vane karoti;

Sā kassa kandāmi vanassa majjhe, yo tāyitā so sahasaṃ sahasā (sī. syā. pī.) karotīti.

He who should be a refuge for one afflicted by suffering—that father of mine—harms me in the forest. To whom shall I cry in the middle of the forest, when he who should be my protector commits violence?

Paṇṇikajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Paṇṇika Jātaka, the Second.

103. Verijātakaṃ

103. The Veri Jātaka

103.

103.

Yattha [T 1.0034] verī nivisati nivasati (sī. ka.), na vase tattha paṇḍito;

Ekarattaṃ dirattaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vasati verisūti.

A wise person should not dwell where an enemy lives; it is painful to live among enemies, even for one night or two.

Verijātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Veri Jātaka, the Third.

104. Mittavindakajātakaṃ

104. The Mittavindaka Jātaka

104.

104.

Catubbhi aṭṭhajjhagamā, aṭṭhāhipi ca soḷasa;

Soḷasāhi ca bāttiṃsa battiṃsa (sī. syā. pī.), atricchaṃ cakkamāsado;

Icchāhatassa posassa, cakkaṃ bhamati matthaketi.

From four you obtained eight, and from eight, sixteen; from sixteen, thirty-two. Through excessive greed, you have come upon the wheel. Upon the head of a person struck by craving, the wheel spins.

Mittavindakajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Mittavindaka Jātaka, the Fourth.

105. Dubbalakaṭṭhajātakaṃ

105. The Dubbalakaṭṭha Jātaka

105.

105.

Bahumpetaṃ [V 1.0024][M 1.0025] vane kaṭṭhaṃ, vāto bhañjati dubbalaṃ;

Tassa ce bhāyasī nāga, kiso nūna bhavissasīti.

O great elephant, in the forest the wind breaks this weak wood, though it is plentiful. If you fear that sound, you will surely become lean.

Dubbalakaṭṭhajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Dubbalakaṭṭha Jātaka, the Fifth.

106. Udañcanījātakaṃ

106. The Udañcanī Jātaka

106.

106.

Sukhaṃ vata maṃ jīvantaṃ sukhakaṃ vata jīvaṃ (ka.), pacamānā udañcanī;

Corī jāyappavādena, telaṃ loṇañca yācatīti.

Indeed, while I am living happily, this tormenting thief-woman, like a water-pot, entices me with pleasant speech and asks for oil and salt.

Udañcanījātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Udañcanī Jātaka, the Sixth.

107. Sālittakajātakaṃ

107. The Sālittaka Jātaka

107.

107.

Sādhu [T 1.0035] kho sippakaṃ nāma, api yādisa kīdisaṃ;

Passa khañjappahārena, laddhā gāmā catuddisāti.

Indeed, any art soever, of whatever kind, is good. Behold! By the cripple's throw, villages in the four directions were obtained.

Sālittakajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Sālittaka Jātaka, the Seventh.

108. Bāhiyajātakaṃ

108. The Bāhiya Jātaka

108.

108.

Sikkheyya sikkhitabbāni, santi tacchandino sacchandino (sī. pī.) janā;

Bāhiyā hi pi (sī. syā. pī.) suhannena, rājānamabhirādhayīti.

One should learn the arts that ought to be learned; there are people who desire them. Indeed, the man from the outer country pleased the king with a well-covered body-wipe.

Bāhiyajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Bāhiya Jātaka, the Eighth.

109. Kuṇḍapūvajātakaṃ

109. The Kuṇḍapūva Jātaka

109.

109.

Yathanno puriso hoti, tathannā tassa devatā;

Āharetaṃ kuṇḍapūvaṃ kaṇaṃ pūvaṃ (sī. pī.), mā me bhāgaṃ vināsayāti.

As is the food of a man, so is the food of his deity. Bring this broken-rice cake; do not destroy my share.

Kuṇḍapūvajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Kuṇḍapūva Jātaka, the Ninth.

110. Sabbasaṃhārakapañhajātakaṃ

110. The Sabbasaṃhāraka-pañha Jātaka

110.

110.

Sabbasaṃhārako [V 1.0025][M 1.0026] sabbasāhārako (ka.) natthi, suddhaṃ kaṅgu pavāyati;

Alikaṃ bhāyatiyaṃ dhuttī, saccamāha mahallikāti.

The Sabbasāhāraka perfume does not exist; only pure kaṅgu perfume is fragrant. This young rogue speaks a falsehood; this old woman spoke the truth.

Sabbasaṃhārakapañhajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Sabbasaṃhāraka-pañha Jātaka, the Tenth.

Parosatavaggo ekādasamo.

The Parosata Vagga, the Eleventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary thereof:

Saparosata tāyita verī [T 1.0036] puna, bhamacakkatha nāgasirivhayano;

Sukhakañca vata sippaka bāhiyā, kuṇḍapūva mahallikakā ca dasāti.

The Parosata, Paṇṇika, and Verī Jātakas; again, the Mittavindaka and Dubbalakaṭṭha Jātakas; the Udañcanī, Sālittaka, and Bāhira Jātakas; and the Kuṇḍapūva and Mahallikā Jātakas—these are the ten.

12. Haṃcivaggo

12. The Haṃci Vagga

111. Gadrabhapañhajātakaṃ

111. The Gadrabhapañha Jātaka

111.

111.

Haṃci haṃsi (sī. syā.), hañci (?) tuvaṃ evamaññasi seyyo, puttena pitāti rājaseṭṭha;

Handassatarassa te ayaṃ, assatarassa hi gadrabho pitāti.

O best of kings, if you indeed think thus, 'The father is superior to the son,' then let this donkey be superior to your mule; for the donkey is the father of the mule.

Gadrabhapañhajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Gadrabhapañha Jātaka, the First.

112. Amarādevīpañhajātakaṃ

112. The Amarādevīpañha Jātaka

112.

112.

Yena sattubilaṅgā ca, diguṇapalāso ca pupphito;

Yena dadāmi yenā’dāmi (sī. syā.) tena vadāmi, yena na dadāmi yena nā’dāmi (sī. syā.) na tena vadāmi;

Esa [T 1.0037] maggo yavamajjhakassa, etaṃ channapathaṃ vijānāhīti.

Where there are roasted grain cakes and a flowering, double-leafed palāsa tree; with that by which I give, I speak; with that by which I do not give, I do not speak. This is the path to Yavamajjhaka; know this hidden path.

Amarādevīpañhajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Amarādevīpañha Jātaka, the Second.

113. Siṅgālajātakaṃ

113. The Siṅgāla Jātaka

113.

113.

Saddahāsi [M 1.0027] siṅgālassa sigālassa (sī. syā. pī.), surāpītassa brāhmaṇa;

Sippikānaṃ sataṃ natthi, kuto kaṃsasatā duveti.

O Brahmin, do you believe the word of a jackal that has drunk liquor? It does not possess a hundred spoons; whence could it have two hundred bronze coins?

Siṅgālajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Siṅgāla Jātaka, the Third.

114. Mitacintijātakaṃ

114. The Mitacintī Jātaka

114.

114.

Bahucintī [V 1.0026] appacintī, ubho jāle abajjhare;

Mitacintī pamocesī, ubho tattha samāgatāti.

Bahucintī and Appacintī were both caught in the net. Mitacintī effected their release; the two were reunited there.

Mitacintijātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Mitacintī Jātaka, the Fourth.

115. Anusāsikajātakaṃ

115. The Anusāsikā Jātaka

115.

115.

Yāyañña yāyaññe (ka.) manusāsati, sayaṃ loluppacārinī;

Sāyaṃ vipakkhikā seti, hatā cakkena sāsikāti sālikāti (sī. syā. pī.).

She who admonishes others, while herself being of fickle conduct—that very instructress lies with severed wings, having been struck by a wheel.

Anusāsikajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Anusāsikā Jātaka, the Fifth.

116. Dubbacajātakaṃ

116. The Dubbaca Jātaka

116.

116.

Atikaramakarācariya[T 1.0038], mayhampetaṃ na ruccati;

Catutthe laṅghayitvāna, pañcamāyasi āvutoti.

O teacher, you have done an excessive deed; this does not please me either. Having jumped over the fourth, you are pierced by the fifth.

Dubbacajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Dubbaca Jātaka, the Sixth.

117. Tittirajātakaṃ

117. The Tittira Jātaka

117.

117.

Accuggatātilapatā atibalatā (sī. syā. pī.), atilapakā (katthaci), ativelaṃ pabhāsitā;

Vācā hanati dummedhaṃ, tittiraṃvātivassitanti.

Speech that is too lofty, too repetitive, and spoken beyond measure, kills the fool, just as excessive rain kills the partridge.

Tittirajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Tittira Jātaka, the Seventh.

118. Vaṭṭakajātakaṃ

118. The Vaṭṭaka Jātaka

118.

118.

Nācintayanto puriso, visesamadhigacchati;

Cintitassa phalaṃ passa, muttosmi vadhabandhanāti.

A man who does not reflect does not attain a special state. Behold the fruit of reflection: I am freed from death and bondage!

Vaṭṭakajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Vaṭṭaka Jātaka, the Eighth.

119. Akālarāvijātakaṃ

119. The Akālarāvi Jātaka

119.

119.

Amātāpitarasaṃvaddho [M 1.0028] pitari (sī. pī.), pitu (syā.), anācerakule vasaṃ;

Nāyaṃ kālaṃ akālaṃ vā, abhijānāti kukkuṭoti.

Reared without the instruction of mother and father, living in a household with no teacher, this rooster does not know the right time or the wrong time.

Akālarāvijātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Akālarāvi Jātaka, the Ninth.

120. Bandhanamokkhajātakaṃ

120. The Bandhanamokkha Jātaka

120.

120.

Abaddhā [T 1.0039][V 1.0027] tattha bajjhanti, yattha bālā pabhāsare;

Baddhāpi tattha muccanti, yattha dhīrā pabhāsareti.

Where fools speak, the unbound are bound; where the wise speak, even the bound are freed.

Bandhanamokkhajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Bandhanamokkha Jātaka, the Tenth.

Haṃcivaggo haṃsivaggo (sī. syā.) dvādasamo.

The Haṃci Chapter, the Twelfth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Atha gadrabha sattuva kaṃsasataṃ, bahucinti sāsikāyātikara;

Ativela visesamanācariyova, dhīrāpabhāsaratena dasāti.

Then, the Donkey, Roasted Grain, a Hundred Kamsas, Bahucintī, the Instructress, the Excessive Deed; Beyond Measure, Distinction, Without a Teacher, and the Wise Speak Forth—these are the ten.

13. Kusanāḷivaggo

13. The Kusanāḷi Chapter

121. Kusanāḷijātakaṃ

121. The Kusanāḷi Jātaka

121.

121.

Kare sarikkho atha vāpi seṭṭho, nihīnako vāpi kareyya eko;

Kareyyumete kareyyuṃ te (sī. pī.) byasane uttamatthaṃ, yathā ahaṃ kusanāḷi rucāyanti.

Let an equal, or a superior, or even a single inferior person act. In calamity, they would achieve the highest good, just as I in the Rucā tree and Kusanāḷi have done.

Kusanāḷijātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Kusanāḷi Jātaka, the First.

122. Dummedhajātakaṃ

122. The Dummedha Jātaka

122.

122.

Yasaṃ [T 1.0040][M 1.0029] laddhāna dummedho, anatthaṃ carati attano;

Attano ca paresañca, hiṃsāya paṭipajjatīti.

Having gained prosperity, the fool acts to his own detriment; he proceeds to the harm of both himself and others.

Dummedhajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Dummedha Jātaka, the Second.

123. Naṅgalīsajātakaṃ

123. The Naṅgalīsa Jātaka

123.

123.

Asabbatthagāmiṃ vācaṃ, bālo sabbattha bhāsati;

Nāyaṃ dadhiṃ vedi na na vedi (ka.) naṅgalīsaṃ, dadhippayaṃ dadhimpayaṃ (sī. pī.) maññati naṅgalīsanti.

The fool utters speech that is not universally applicable in every instance. This one knows neither curd nor a ploughshare; he thinks even curd is a ploughshare.

Naṅgalīsajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Naṅgalīsa Jātaka, the Third.

124. Ambajātakaṃ

124. The Amba Jātaka

124.

124.

Vāyametheva [V 1.0028] puriso, na nibbindeyya paṇḍito;

Vāyāmassa phalaṃ passa, bhuttā ambā anītihanti.

A man should indeed strive; a wise man should not become discouraged. Behold the fruit of striving: mangoes were eaten without affliction.

Ambajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Amba Jātaka, the Fourth.

125. Kaṭāhakajātakaṃ

125. The Kaṭāhaka Jātaka

125.

125.

Bahumpi so vikattheyya, aññaṃ janapadaṃ gato;

Anvāgantvāna dūseyya, bhuñja bhoge kaṭāhakāti.

Having gone to another country, he may boast much; and upon returning, he may cause corruption. Enjoy your possessions, O Kaṭāhaka!

Kaṭāhakajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Kaṭāhaka Jātaka, the Fifth.

126. Asilakkhaṇajātakaṃ

126. The Asilakkhaṇa Jātaka

126.

126.

Tadevekassa [T 1.0041] tathevekassa (sī. syā. pī. aṭṭha. mūlapāṭho) kalyāṇaṃ, tadevekassa pāpakaṃ;

Tasmā sabbaṃ na kalyāṇaṃ, sabbaṃ vāpi na pāpakanti.

That very same thing is good for one, and that very same thing is bad for another. Therefore, not everything is good, nor is everything bad.

Asilakkhaṇajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Asilakkhaṇa Jātaka, the Sixth.

127. Kalaṇḍukajātakaṃ

127. The Kalaṇḍuka Jātaka

127.

127.

Te desā tāni vatthūni, ahañca vanagocaro;

Anuvicca kho taṃ gaṇheyyuṃ, piva pipa (sī. pī.) khīraṃ kalaṇḍukāti.

Those are the regions, those are the abodes, and I am a forest-dweller. Having investigated, they would surely seize you. Drink the milk, O Kalaṇḍuka!

Kalaṇḍukajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Kalaṇḍuka Jātaka, the Seventh.

128. Biḷāravatajātakaṃ

128. The Biḷāravata Jātaka

128.

128.

Yo [M 1.0030] ve dhammaṃ dhajaṃ dhammadhajaṃ (syā. pī. ka.) katvā, nigūḷho pāpamācare;

Vissāsayitvā bhūtāni, biḷāraṃ nāma taṃ vatanti.

Whoever, having made the Dhamma his banner, secretly commits evil while having gained the trust of beings—that practice is called the cat's vow.

Biḷāravatajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Biḷāravata Jātaka, the eighth.

129. Aggikabhāradvājajātakaṃ

129. The Aggikabhāradvāja Jātaka

129.

129.

Nāyaṃ sikhā puññahetu, ghāsahetu ayaṃ sikhā;

Nāṅguṭṭhagaṇanaṃ yāti, alaṃ te hotu aggikāti.

This top-knot is not for the sake of merit; this top-knot is for the sake of food. It comes to a counting of tails. Let that be enough for you, O Aggika!

Aggikabhāradvājajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Aggikabhāradvāja Jātaka, the ninth.

130. Kosiyajātakaṃ

130. The Kosiya Jātaka

130.

130.

Yathā [T 1.0042][V 1.0029] vācā ca bhuñjassu, yathā bhuttañca byāhara;

Ubhayaṃ te na sameti, vācā bhuttañca kosiyeti.

Eat according to your speech, and speak according to what you have eaten. Your speech and your eating do not accord, O Kosiya.

Kosiyajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Kosiya Jātaka, the tenth.

Kusanāḷivaggo sarikkhavaggo (ka.) terasamo.

The Kusanāḷi Vagga, the thirteenth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Kusanāḷisirivhayano ca yasaṃ, dadhi mamba kaṭāhakapañcamako;

Atha pāpaka khīra biḷāravataṃ, sikhi kosiyasavhayanena dasāti.

Kusanāḷi, Sirivhayana, and Yasaṃ; Dadhi, Amba, and Kaṭāhaka as the fifth; then Pāpaka, Khīra, Biḷāravata; Sikhi, and with the one named Kosiya, there are ten.

14. Asampadānavaggo

14. The Asampadāna Vagga

131. Asampadānajātakaṃ

131. The Asampadāna Jātaka.

131.

131.

Asampadānenitarītarassa, bālassa mittāni kalī bhavanti;

Tasmā harāmi bhusaṃ aḍḍhamānaṃ, mā me mitti jīyittha sassatāyanti.

Through not giving, the friendships of a common fool are destroyed. Therefore, I bring a half-measure of chaff, thinking, 'May my friendship not perish, but be eternal.'

Asampadānajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Asampadāna Jātaka, the first.

132. Bhīrukajātakaṃ

132. The Bhīruka Jātaka

132.

132.

Kusalūpadese [T 1.0043][M 1.0031] dhitiyā daḷhāya ca, anivattitattābhayabhīrutāya avatthitattābhayabhīrutāya (sī. syā. pī.) ca;

Na rakkhasīnaṃ vasamāgamimhase, sa sotthibhāvo mahatā bhayena meti.

Through the instruction of the skilled, through firm fortitude, and by not turning back from fear and terror, we did not come under the power of the ogresses. That state of well-being arose for me from great fear.

Bhīruka pañcagaruka (sī. pī.), pañcabhīruka (syā.), abhayabhīruta§(?) jātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Bhīruka Jātaka, the second.

133. Ghatāsanajātakaṃ

133. The Ghatāsana Jātaka

133.

133.

Khemaṃ yahiṃ tattha arī udīrito ari uddharito (ka.), dakassa majjhe jalate ghatāsano;

Na ajja vāso mahiyā mahīruhe, disā bhajavho saraṇājja no bhayanti.

Where it was safe, there the enemy has arisen. In the middle of the water, the fire blazes. Today there is no dwelling for us in the tree grown from the earth. Flee to the directions! Today, fear has arisen for us from our refuge.

Ghatāsanajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Ghatāsana Jātaka, the third.

134. Jhānasodhanajātakaṃ

134. The Jhānasodhana Jātaka

134.

134.

Ye [V 1.0030] saññino tepi duggatā, yepi asaññino tepi duggatā;

Etaṃ ubhayaṃ vivajjaya, taṃ [T 1.0044] samāpattisukhaṃ anaṅgaṇanti.

Those who are percipient are in a woeful state, and those who are non-percipient are also in a woeful state. Having avoided both of these, that bliss of attainment is without blemish.

Jhānasodhanajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Jhānasodhana Jātaka, the fourth.

135. Candābhajātakaṃ

135. The Candābha Jātaka

135.

135.

Candābhaṃ sūriyābhañca, yodha paññāya gādhati.

Avitakkena jhānena, hoti ābhassarūpagoti.

Whoever here with wisdom fathoms the moon's splendor and the sun's splendor, through the jhāna without initial thought, becomes one who goes to the Ābhassara realm.

Candābhajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Candābha Jātaka, the fifth.

136. Suvaṇṇahaṃsajātakaṃ

136. The Suvaṇṇahaṃsa Jātaka

136.

136.

Yaṃ [M 1.0032] laddhaṃ tena tuṭṭhabbaṃ, atilobho hi pāpako;

Haṃsarājaṃ gahetvāna, suvaṇṇā parihāyathāti.

One should be content with what has been obtained, for excessive greed is indeed evil. Having seized the goose-king, you were deprived of gold.

Suvaṇṇahaṃsajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Suvaṇṇahaṃsa Jātaka, the sixth.

137. Babbujātakaṃ

137. The Babbu Jātaka

137.

137.

Yattheko labhate babbu, dutiyo tattha jāyati;

Tatiyo ca catuttho ca, idaṃ te babbukā bilanti.

Where one cat obtains something, a second appears there, and a third, and a fourth. This, for those cats, is their cave.

Babbujātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Babbu Jātaka, the seventh.

138. Godhajātakaṃ

138. The Godha Jātaka

138.

138.

Kiṃ te jaṭāhi dummedha, kiṃ te ajinasāṭiyā;

Abbhantaraṃ [T 1.0045] te gahanaṃ, bāhiraṃ parimajjasīti.

What use are your matted locks to you, O foolish one? What use is your deerskin garment? Inside you is a thicket, while you polish the outside.

Godhajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Godha Jātaka, the eighth.

139. Ubhatobhaṭṭhajātakaṃ

139. The Ubhatobhaṭṭha Jātaka

139.

139.

Akkhī bhinnā paṭo naṭṭho, sakhigehe ca bhaṇḍanaṃ;

Ubhato paduṭṭhā kammantā paduṭṭhakammanto (sī.), paduṭṭho kammanto (pī.), udakamhi thalamhi cāti.

Your eye is pierced, your cloth is lost, and at home there is a quarrel with your wife. Your undertakings are ruined in both places, on water and on land.

Ubhatobhaṭṭhajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ubhatobhaṭṭha Jātaka, the ninth.

140. Kākajātakaṃ

140. The Kāka Jātaka

140.

140.

Niccaṃ [V 1.0031] ubbiggahadayā, sabbalokavihesakā;

Tasmā nesaṃ vasā natthi, kākānamhāka kākānasmāka (sī. syā. pī.) ñātinanti.

Always with agitated hearts, tormentors of the whole world; therefore, for those crows, our kinsmen, there is no fat.

Kākajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Kaka Jataka, the tenth.

Asampadānavaggo cuddasamo.

The Asampadāna Vagga, the fourteenth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof is:

Itarītara [M 1.0033] rakkhasi khemiyo ca, parosatapañhena ābhassaro puna;

Atha haṃsavaruttamababbujaṭaṃ, paṭanaṭṭhaka kākavarena dasāti.

The Asampadāna, Bhīruka, and Ghaṭāsana; again, Candābha with Jhānasodhana; then Suvaṇṇahaṃsa, Babbu, and Godha, together with Ubhatobhaṭṭha and the excellent Kaka—these are the ten.

15. Kakaṇṭakavaggo

15. The Kakaṇṭaka Vagga

141. Godhajātakaṃ

141. The Godha Jataka

141.

141.

Na [T 1.0046] pāpajanasaṃsevī, accantasukhamedhati;

Godhākulaṃ godhakkulaṃ (ka.) kakaṇṭāva kakaṇṭakā (ka.), kaliṃ pāpeti attananti.

One who associates with evil people does not attain ultimate happiness; like the iguana family with the chameleon, one brings oneself to ruin.

Godhajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Godha Jataka, the first.

142. Siṅgālajātakaṃ

142. The Siṅgāla Jataka

142.

142.

Etañhi te durājānaṃ, yaṃ sesi matasāyikaṃ;

Yassa te kaḍḍhamānassa, hatthā daṇḍo na muccatīti.

This of yours is indeed difficult to know: why you lie as if dead, and why, as you are being dragged, the staff is not released from your hand.

Siṅgālajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Siṅgāla Jataka, the second.

143. Virocajātakaṃ

143. The Viroca Jataka

143.

143.

Lasī ca te nipphalitā, matthako ca padālito vidālito (sī. pī.);

Sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā, ajja kho tvaṃ virocasīti.

Your brain has burst forth, and your head is split open; all your ribs are broken—now, indeed, you shine!

Virocajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Viroca Jataka, the third.

144. Naṅguṭṭhajātakaṃ

144. The Naṅguṭṭha Jataka

144.

144.

Bahumpetaṃ [V 1.0032] asabbhi bahupetamasabbhi (ka.) jātaveda, yaṃ taṃ vāladhinābhipūjayāma;

Maṃsārahassa [T 1.0047] natthajja maṃsaṃ, naṅguṭṭhampi bhavaṃ paṭiggahātūti.

This is a great thing, O ignoble Jātaveda, that we worship you with a tail. For you, who are worthy of meat, there is no meat today. May your honor accept even a tail.

Naṅguṭṭhajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Naṅguṭṭha Jataka, the fourth.

145. Rādhajātakaṃ

145. The Rādha Jataka

145.

145.

Na [M 1.0034] tvaṃ rādha vijānāsi, aḍḍharatte anāgate;

Abyayataṃ abyāyataṃ (sī. syā. pī.), abyattataṃ (?) vilapasi, virattā kosiyāyaneti.

O Rādha, you do not understand. With midnight not yet arrived, you lament unskillfully that Kosiyāyanī is dispassionate.

Rādhajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Rādha Jataka, the fifth.

146. Samuddakākajātakaṃ

146. The Samuddakāka Jataka

146.

146.

Api nu hanukā santā, mukhañca parisussati;

Oramāma na pārema, pūrateva mahodadhīti.

Indeed, our jaws are weary and our mouths are parched. We try to empty it but cannot succeed; the great ocean just keeps filling up.

Samuddakākajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Samuddakāka Jataka, the sixth.

147. Puppharattajātakaṃ

147. The Puppharatta Jataka

147.

147.

Nayidaṃ dukkhaṃ aduṃ dukkhaṃ, yaṃ maṃ tudati vāyaso;

Yaṃ sāmā puppharattena, kattikaṃ nānubhossatīti.

This is not suffering, that the crow pecks me; that Sāmā will not enjoy the Kattika festival in her flower-dyed robe—that is suffering.

Puppharattajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Puppharatta Jataka, the seventh.

148. Siṅgālajātakaṃ

148. The Siṅgāla Jataka

148.

148.

Nāhaṃ [T 1.0048] punaṃ na ca punaṃ, na cāpi apunappunaṃ;

Hatthibondiṃ pavekkhāmi, tathā hi bhayatajjitoti.

I shall not again, nor again, nor yet again and again, enter an elephant's carcass, for I was so terrified by fear.

Siṅgālajātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Siṅgāla Jataka, the eighth.

149. Ekapaṇṇajātakaṃ

149. The Ekapaṇṇa Jataka

149.

149.

Ekapaṇṇo ayaṃ rukkho, na bhūmyā caturaṅgulo;

Phalena visakappena, mahāyaṃ kiṃ bhavissatīti.

This tree is one-leafed, not four fingers high from the ground; with fruit like a deadly poison, what will it become when it is large?

Ekapaṇṇajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Ekapaṇṇa Jataka, the ninth.

150. Sañjīvajātakaṃ

150. The Sañjīva Jataka

150.

150.

Asantaṃ [V 1.0033][M 1.0035] yo paggaṇhāti, asantaṃ cūpasevati;

Tameva ghāsaṃ kurute, byaggho sañjīvako yathāti.

Whoever honors an unvirtuous person and associates with the unvirtuous, that very unvirtuous one makes a meal of him, just as the tiger did of Sañjīva.

Sañjīvajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Sañjīva Jataka, the tenth.

Kakaṇṭaka pāpasevana (ka.) vaggo pannarasamo.

The Kakaṇṭaka Vagga, the fifteenth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sukhamedhati daṇḍavaro ca puna, lasi vāladhi pañcamarādhavaro;

Samahodadhi [T 1.0049] kattika bondi puna, caturaṅgulabyagghavarena dasāti.

The Godha, the first Siṅgāla, again Viroca, Naṅguṭṭha, and the excellent Rādha as the fifth; Samuddakāka, Puppharatta, the second Siṅgāla; again, with Ekapaṇṇa and the excellent Sañjīva, these are the ten.

(Uparimo paṇṇāsako.) ( ) sīhaḷapotthakeyeva dissati

(The Upper Fifty.)

Atha vagguddānaṃ –

Then the summary of the chapters:

Apaṇṇakaṃ sīlavaggakuruṅga, kulāvakaṃ atthakāmena pañcamaṃ;

Āsīso itthivaruṇaṃ apāyi, littavaggena te dasa;

Parosataṃ haṃci kusanāḷi haṃsi sarikkhaṃ (sabbattha), asampadaṃ kakaṇṭakavaggo.

The Apaṇṇaka, Sīlavagga, Kuruṅga, Kulāvaka, with Atthakāma as the fifth; Āsīsa, Itthi, Varuṇa, Apāyi, and with the Litta chapter, they are ten; Parosata, Haṃci, Kusanāḷi, Asampada, and the Kakaṇṭaka chapter.

Ekanipātamhilaṅkatanti.

By these, the Ekanipāta is adorned.

Ekakanipātaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Book of Ones is finished.

2. Dukanipāto

2. The Book of Twos

1. Daḷhavaggo

1. The Daḷha Chapter

151. Rājovādajātakaṃ (2-1-1)

151. The Rājovāda Jātaka (2-1-1)

1.

1.

Daḷhaṃ [T 1.0050][V 1.0034][M 1.0036] daḷhassa khipati, balliko malliko (sī. pī.) mudunā muduṃ;

Sādhumpi sādhunā jeti, asādhumpi asādhunā;

Etādiso ayaṃ rājā, maggā uyyāhi sārathi.

King Ballika imposes harshness upon the harsh; he conquers the gentle with gentleness. He conquers the good with goodness, and the bad with badness. Such is this king; O charioteer, move aside from the path.

2.

2.

Akkodhena jine kodhaṃ, asādhuṃ sādhunā jine;

Jine kadariyaṃ dānena, saccenālikavādinaṃ;

Etādiso ayaṃ rājā, maggā uyyāhi sārathīti.

He conquers the angry with non-anger, the unvirtuous with goodness; he conquers the stingy with giving, and the speaker of falsehood with truth. Such is this king; O charioteer, move aside from the path.

Rājovādajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Rājovāda Jātaka, the First.

152. Asamekkhitakammantaṃ, turitābhinipātinaṃ.

152. For one who acts without reflection, who rushes hastily,

Sāni kammāni tappenti, uṇhaṃvajjhohitaṃ mukhe.

those deeds bring torment, like something hot placed in the mouth.

4.

4.

Sīho ca sīhanādena, daddaraṃ abhinādayi;

Sutvā sīhassa nigghosaṃ, siṅgālo sigālo (sī. syā. pī.) daddare vasaṃ;

Bhīto santāsamāpādi, hadayañcassa apphalīti.

And the lion, with its lion's roar, made the mountain resound. Hearing the lion's fierce roar, the jackal dwelling on the mountain became frightened, fell into terror, and its heart burst.

Siṅgālajātakaṃ sigālajātakaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) dutiyaṃ.

The Siṅgāla Jātaka, the Second.

153. Sūkarajātakaṃ (2-1-3)

153. The Sūkara Jātaka (2-1-3)

5.

5.

Catuppado [T 1.0051] ahaṃ samma, tvampi samma catuppado;

Ehi samma sīha (sī. pī.) nivattassu, kiṃ nu bhīto palāyasi.

153. I am four-footed, friend, and you too, friend, are four-footed. Come, friend, turn back! Why do you flee in fear?

6.

6.

Asuci [V 1.0035] pūtilomosi, duggandho vāsi sūkara;

Sace yujjhitukāmosi, jayaṃ samma dadāmi teti.

You are impure, with foul-smelling hair, and you stink, O boar. If you wish to fight, friend, I grant you the victory.

Sūkarajātakaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Sūkara Jātaka, the Third.

154. Uragajātaka (2-1-4)

154. The Uraga Jātaka (2-1-4)

7.

7.

Idhūragānaṃ [M 1.0037] pavaro paviṭṭho, selassa vaṇṇena pamokkhamicchaṃ;

Brahmañca vaṇṇaṃ vakkaṃ (ka.) apacāyamāno, bubhukkhito no vitarāmi visahāmi (ka. si. syā. pī.) bhottuṃ.

Here the most excellent of nāgas has entered, desiring release, in the guise of a jewel. And I, revering the noble robe, though famished, do not dare to eat him.

8.

8.

So brahmagutto cirameva jīva, dibyā ca te pātubhavantu bhakkhā;

Yo brahmavaṇṇaṃ apacāyamāno, bubhukkhito no vitarāsi sabbatthapi samānaṃ bhottunti.

154. May you, protected by what is holy, live for a very long time, and may divine foods appear for you—you who, revering the noble robe, though famished, do not dare to eat.

Uragajātakaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Uraga Jātaka, the Fourth.

155. Bhaggajātakaṃ (2-1-5)

155. The Bhagga Jātaka (2-1-5)

9.

9.

Jīva [T 1.0052] vassasataṃ bhagga gagga (sī. pī.), aparāni ca vīsatiṃ vīsati (syā. ka.);

Mā maṃ pisācā khādantu, jīva tvaṃ sarado sataṃ.

O Bhagga, may you live for a hundred years, and for another twenty; may pisācas not devour me, may you live for a hundred autumns.

10.

10.

Tvampi vassasataṃ jīva, aparāni ca vīsatiṃ;

Visaṃ pisācā khādantu, jīva tvaṃ sarado satanti.

May you too live for a hundred years, and for another twenty; may the pisācas devour poison, may you live for a hundred autumns.

Bhaggajātakaṃ pañcamaṃ.

155. The Bhagga Jātaka, the Fifth.

156. Alīnacittajātakaṃ (2-1-6)

The Jātaka of the Undaunted Mind (2-1-6)

11.

11.

Alīnacittaṃ nissāya, pahaṭṭhā mahatī camū;

Kosalaṃ senāsantuṭṭhaṃ, jīvaggāhaṃ agāhayi.

Relying on Alīnacitta, the great and delighted army captured the discontented Kosalan king alive.

12.

12.

Evaṃ nissayasampanno, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo;

Bhāvayaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, yogakkhemassa pattiyā;

Pāpuṇe anupubbena, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayanti.

Thus a monk, endowed with support and with aroused energy, cultivating the wholesome Dhamma for the attainment of security from the yokes, would gradually attain the destruction of all fetters.

Alīnacittajātakaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

156. The Alīnacitta Jātaka, the Sixth.

157. Guṇajātakaṃ (2-1-7)

157. The Guṇa Jātaka (2-1-7)

13.

13.

Yena [M 1.0038] kāmaṃ paṇāmeti, dhammo balavataṃ migī;

Unnadantī vijānāhi, jātaṃ saraṇato bhayaṃ.

O queen of beasts with upturned tusks, know this: a powerful one sends away whomever he wishes; this is the nature of the powerful. Fear has arisen from our refuge.

14.

14.

Api [V 1.0036] cepi dubbalo mitto, mittadhammesu tiṭṭhati;

So ñātako ca bandhu ca, so mitto so ca me sakhā;

Dāṭhini [T 1.0053] mātimaññittho maññivo (syā.), maññavho (ka.), siṅgālo mama pāṇadoti.

O lioness, even if a friend is weak, if he abides by the principles of friendship, he is my kinsman and relative, he is my friend and my companion. Do not despise the jackal, for he is the giver of my life.

Guṇajātakaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Guṇa Jātaka, the Seventh.

158. Suhanujātakaṃ (2-1-8)

158. The Suhanu Jātaka (2-1-8)

15.

15.

Nayidaṃ visamasīlena, soṇena suhanū saha;

Suhanūpi tādisoyeva, yo soṇassa sagocaro.

157. This is not right, Suhanu with the ill-behaved Soṇa. For Suhanu becomes just like Soṇa, whose companion he is.

16.

16.

Pakkhandinā pagabbhena, niccaṃ sandānakhādinā;

Sameti pāpaṃ pāpena, sameti asatā asanti.

With the impetuous, the insolent, the one who always chews his tether, evil meets with evil, the unrighteous meets with the unrighteous.

Suhanujātakaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Suhanu Jātaka, the Eighth.

159. Morajātakaṃ (2-1-9)

159. The Mora Jātaka (2-1-9)

17.

17.

Udetayaṃ cakkhumā ekarājā, harissavaṇṇo pathavippabhāso paṭhavippabhāso (sī. syā. pī.);

Taṃ taṃ namassāmi harissavaṇṇaṃ pathavippabhāsaṃ, tayājja guttā viharemu divasaṃ.

Arising is this one, the Eye, the sole sovereign, golden-hued, illuminating the earth. Him I worship, the golden-hued one, illuminating the earth; protected by you today, may we dwell throughout the day.

Ye brāhmaṇā vedagū sabbadhamme, te me namo te ca maṃ pālayantu;

Namatthu buddhānaṃ buddhāna (?) namatthu bodhiyā, namo vimuttānaṃ vimuttāna (?) namo vimuttiyā;

Imaṃ so parittaṃ katvā, moro carati esanā.

158. Those brāhmaṇas who have gone to the end of knowledge in all things, to them be my homage, and may they protect me. Homage be to the Buddhas, homage be to enlightenment. Homage to the liberated ones, homage to liberation. Having made this protective chant, the peacock goes in search of food.

18.

18.

Apetayaṃ [T 1.0054][M 1.0039] cakkhumā ekarājā, harissavaṇṇo pathavippabhāso;

Taṃ taṃ nammassāmi harissavaṇṇaṃ pathavippabhāsaṃ, tayājja guttā viharemu rattiṃ.

Departing is this one, the Eye, the sole sovereign, golden-hued, illuminating the earth. To him I pay homage, the golden-hued one, illuminating the earth; protected by you today, may we dwell throughout the night.

Ye brāhmaṇā vedagū sabbadhamme, te me namo te ca maṃ pālayantu;

Namatthu buddhānaṃ namatthu bodhiyā, namo vimuttānaṃ namo vimuttiyā;

Imaṃ so parittaṃ katvā, moro vāsamakappayīti.

Those who are brāhmaṇas, who have gone to the end of knowledge in all things, to them be my homage, and may they protect me. Homage be to the Buddhas, homage be to enlightenment. Homage to the liberated ones, homage to liberation. Having made this protective chant, the peacock took up his dwelling.

Morajātakaṃ navamaṃ.

The Mora Jātaka, the ninth.

160. Vinīlajātakaṃ (2-1-10)

160. The Vinīlaka Jātaka (2.1.10)

19.

19.

Evameva nūna nu (ka.) rājānaṃ, vedehaṃ mithilaggahaṃ;

Assā vahanti ājaññā, yathā haṃsā vinīlakaṃ.

Indeed, just as thoroughbred steeds carry the king of Vedeha, who has taken up residence in Mithilā, even so do these geese carry me, Vinīlaka.

20.

20.

Vinīla [V 1.0037] duggaṃ bhajasi, abhūmiṃ tāta sevasi;

Gāmantakāni gāmantikāni (sī.), gāmantarāni (ka.) sevassu, etaṃ mātālayaṃ tavāti.

O Vinīlaka, you resort to a difficult place; dear one, you frequent an unsuitable region. You should frequent the outskirts of villages; that is your mother's abode.

Vinīlajātakaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Vinīlaka Jātaka, the tenth.

Daḷhavaggo paṭhamo.

The Daḷha Vagga, the first.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Varaballika [T 1.0055] daddara sūkarako, uragūttama pañcamabhaggavaro;

Mahatīcamu yāva siṅgālavaro, suhanuttama mora vinīlaṃ dasāti.

The Rājovāda, the Siṅgāla, the Sukara, the Suhanu, the Mora, the Uraga, the Bhagga, the Alīnacitta, the Guṇa, and the Vinīlaka Jātakas make ten.

2. Santhavavaggo

2. The Chapter on Association

161. Indasamānagottajātakaṃ (2-2-1)

161. The Indasamānagotta Jātaka (2.2.1)

21.

21.

Na [M 1.0040] santhavaṃ sandhavaṃ (ka.) kāpurisena kayirā, ariyo anariyena pajānamatthaṃ;

Cirānuvutthopi karoti pāpaṃ, gajo yathā indasamānagottaṃ.

A noble one, understanding what is beneficial, should not form an association with a contemptible, ignoble person. For even after living together for a long time, the ignoble one commits evil, just as the elephant did toward Indasamānagotta.

22.

22.

Yaṃ tveva jaññā sadiso mamanti, sīlena paññāya sutena cāpi;

Teneva mettiṃ kayirātha saddhiṃ, sukho have sappurisena saṅgamoti.

Whomever one knows to be similar to oneself in virtue, wisdom, and also in learning, with that very person should one make friends. For association with the good is indeed a happiness.

Indasamānagottajātakaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Indasamānagotta Jātaka, the first.

162. Santhavajātakaṃ (2-2-2)

162. The Santhava Jātaka (2.2.2)

23.

23.

Na [T 1.0056] santhavasmā paramatthi pāpiyo, yo santhavo sandhavo (ka.) kāpurisena hoti;

Santappito sappinā pāyasena pāyāsena (ka.), kicchākataṃ paṇṇakuṭiṃ adayhi adaḍḍhahi (sī. syā.), adaṭṭhahi (pī.), adaddahi (?).

There is nothing more evil than association with a contemptible person. Though satisfied with ghee and milk-rice, it burned down the leaf hut that I made with difficulty.

24.

24.

Na santhavasmā paramatthi seyyo, yo santhavo sappurisena hoti;

Sīhassa byagghassa ca dīpino ca, sāmā mukhaṃ lehati santhavenāti.

There is nothing more excellent than association with a good person. Because of their friendship, the doe licks the faces of the lion, the tiger, and the leopard.

Santhavajātakaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Santhava Jātaka, the second.

163. Susīmajātakaṃ (2-2-3)

163. The Susīma Jātaka (2.2.3)

25.

25.

Kāḷā migā setadantā tavīme tava ime (sī. syā. pī.), parosataṃ hemajālābhichannā hemajālābhisañchannā (sī.);

Te te dadāmīti susīma brūsi, anussaraṃ [T 1.0057] pettipitāmahānaṃ.

These dark beasts with white tusks are yours, more than a hundred, covered with golden nets. Remembering your fathers and grandfathers, O Susīma, you say, 'These very ones I will give away.'

26.

26.

Kāḷā [V 1.0038][M 1.0041] migā setadantā mamīme mama ime (sī. pī.), parosataṃ hemajālābhicchannā;

Te te dadāmīti vadāmi māṇava, anussaraṃ pettipitāmahānanti.
